## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Traffic and Parking Committee Meeting Minutes

Monday, November 9, 2026

6:00 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Sait at 6:04 pm and adjourned at 7:54 pm on a roll call vote of 3 in favor (Councilors Wheeler, Mbah and Sait), 0 opposed, and 0 absent.

Others present: Brian Postlewaite - Director of the Engineering Division, Michael Holland - Somerville Police Lieutenant, Brad Rawson - Director of Transportation and Infrastructure, Suzanne Rinfret - Director of Traffic and Parking, Eric Weisman - Department of Public Works Commissioner, Shumeane Benford - Somerville Police Chief and Delaney Fisher-Cassiol - Clerk of Committees

Roll Call

- Present: City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler, City Councilor At
- Large Wilfred N. Mbah and Ward Five City Councilor
- Naima Sait

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Traffic and Parking Committee Meeting of Minutes

October 5, 2026.

(ID # 26-1518 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, City Councilor At Large
- Mbah and Ward Five City Councilor Sait

2. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Traffic and Paring Committee Meeting of Minutes

October 14, 2026.

(ID # 26-1576 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, City Councilor At Large
- Mbah and Ward Five City Councilor Sait

3. Officer's

Director of Parking conveying information regarding item #26-1019.

Communication

(ID # 26-1090 )

This item was discussed with item #26-1019.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

4. Resolution

By Councilor Wheeler, Councilor Hardt and Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1019 ) That the Director of Parking discuss with this Council the possibility of administering a parking permit type intended for vehicle owners with

driveways, at a lower price than standard residential parking permits, which would allow only daytime and evening street parking but not overnight street

parking, and which would not be usable during street cleaning or snow emergencies.

- Councilor Wheeler noted that he had worked with the Somerville Alliance

for Safe Streets on recommendations highlighted in the 2022 Curb Study regarding a more complex system of parking permits and regulations. He

explained that the goal is to increase parking availability for seniors and people with disabilities, and potentially accommodate additional housing.

- He suggested two permit options: a standard 24-hour permit and a less

expensive daytime-only permit for residents who have access to a driveway and can park there overnight but need to use on-street parking during the day.

- Susanne Rinfret, Director of Parking, noted that administering such a system

would create additional administrative and enforcement burdens. She explained that it would be difficult to determine which residents have

driveway access and that the study also recommended increasing permit costs. Overnight enforcement is limited, with staffing primarily focused on

major areas and street-cleaning enforcement. She added that the department makes a consistent effort to increase the availability of ADA parking spaces. Director Rinfret further explained that Parking Control Officers currently

identify permits by color, and requiring them to verify license plate numbers to distinguish between permit types would make enforcement less efficient

and require additional staff. Councilor Wheeler suggested using a simple visual indicator, such as a dot on the permit, to distinguish between permit

types. He stated that the possibility of receiving a ticket or fine could encourage compliance without requiring extensive enforcement. Director

Rinfret noted that residents with driveways would generally prefer to park in them and that overnight staffing between midnight and 8:00 a.m. is limited.

- She also reiterated the study's recommendation to increase permit costs for

residents with driveway access. She emphasized that the City's broader transportation goals are focused on reducing car dependency through

- improved public transit and walkability.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

5. Resolution

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1424 ) That the Director of Mobility paint bike markings in the bike lane on Elm

Street, across from the Kennedy school.

This item was discussed with item #26-1422.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

6. Resolution

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1423 ) That the Director of Mobility add bike racks at the Kennedy School.

This item was discussed with item #26-1422.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

7. Resolution

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1422 ) That the Director of the Parking install drop-off/pick-up signage on Cherry

Street, across from the Kennedy School.

- Chair Sait thanked the various City departments for working together on
- improvements in the Kennedy School area. Brad Rawson, Director of

Transportation and Infrastructure, reported that the contractor had completed all pavement markings, including the requested bike lane markings, and installed narrower eastbound flexposts that had been delayed due to supply

chain issues. The City continues to welcome public feedback. Additional improvements include new pick-up and drop-off signage on Cherry Street, expanded curb space for quick stops and bike parking on both the sidewalk

- and school grounds. Director Rawson added that a City study found the
- Kennedy School has 30 bike parking spaces, the most of any K-8 school in

Somerville, but additional capacity is still needed. Staff are working on plans to expand bike parking in 2027.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

8. Order

By Councilor Sait, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Clingan, Councilor

(ID # 26-1053 ) Hardt, Councilor Link, Councilor Mbah, Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor

- Scott, Councilor Strezo and Councilor Wheeler

That the Director of Engineering and the Commissioner of Public Works provide an update on Highland Ave temporary paving.

- Brian Postlewaite, Director of the Engineering Division, explained that

temporary paving is not planned for the area because it is already included in the City's five-year paving plan for permanent reconstruction, so the City is prioritizing permanent improvements rather than temporary fixes.

- In response to a question from Councilor Wheeler about potholes, Eric
- Weisman, Department of Public Works Commissioner, noted that the

Streets and Sidewalks Division will begin using milling and overlay for the first time on streets with significant pothole issues.

- In response to a question from Councilor Mbah about paving near Highland

Avenue and Broadway, Director Postlewaite explained that the City is working with utility companies to identify needed infrastructure

improvements and coordinate paving schedules. The streets are included in the City's five-year paving plan. He also noted that the City is conducting a three-year assessment of road and sidewalk conditions. The western side of the City was assessed last year, the central area is being assessed this year and the eastern area will follow. The findings will help the City prioritize

- street reconstruction projects across Somerville.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

9. Order

By Councilor Mbah and Councilor Hardt

(ID # 26-0917 ) That the Director of Mobility, the Director of Engineering, the Director of Parking and the Chief of Police appear before the Traffic and Parking

Committee to review traffic flows and enforcement practices around schools citywide during drop-of and pick-up, as detailed within.

AMENDMENT: That the Director of Mobility, the Director of Engineering, the Director of Parking and the Chief of Police appear before

the Traffic and Parking Committee to review traffic flows and enforcement practices, and construction impacts around schools citywide during drop-of

- and pick-up, as detailed within.

- Councilor Mbah described an incident in which two vehicles were traveling

in opposite directions while children were crossing during school drop-off, which prompted the discussion.

- Brad Rawson, Director of Transportation and Infrastructure, explained that

multiple departments coordinate on school-area traffic safety through monthly Safe Routes meetings focused on pedestrian and bicycle safety, traffic calming and keeping streets safe even when enforcement is not

present. Departments also gather feedback from crossing guards and others working on the streets, improve curb access for pickup and drop-off to discourage illegal stops, coordinate on street accessibility changes and collect traffic and pedestrian data to inform decisions.

- Brian Postlewaite, Director of the Engineering Division, outlined two areas

of the department's work: advancing Safe Streets construction projects, including raised crossings and intersection improvements, and working with

construction companies near schools to limit construction hours during school drop-off and pickup. Suzanne Rinfret, Director of Traffic and Parking, added that the department works to keep traffic moving around

- schools and prevent vehicles from stopping in prohibited areas. Somerville

Police Chief Shumeane Benford explained that the department relies on crossing guards to encourage voluntary compliance. Somerville Police

Lieutenant Michael Holland noted that officers provide additional assistance at the beginning of the school year and during snowstorms to help drivers

- adjust to school-area traffic patterns. Eric Weisman, Department of Public

Works Commissioner, explained that DPW supports these efforts by maintaining facilities, directing contractors such as street sweepers and trash haulers to avoid school zones during drop-off and pickup, and working with

- schools to clear those areas during snowstorms.

- Councilor Mbah expressed appreciation for the interdepartmental

collaboration. In response to a question from Councilor Mbah about school-zone issues, Chief Benford noted that demand will always exceed

available resources, so the department prioritizes known problem locations and responds to complaints. Director Rawson noted that the City maintains

maps of known problem areas during school pickup and drop-off to help allocate resources.

In response to a question from Councilor Wheeler about the intersection of Broadway and McGrath Highway, Chief Benford noted that the intersection

- falls under state jurisdiction and that he was aware of the safety concerns.

- He explained that a study found most pedestrians crossing there were adults

rather than children and noted that a nearby footbridge is available, as recommended through the Safe Routes to School program. In response to a

comment from Chair Sait, he acknowledged that enforcing traffic management requirements at construction sites can be challenging due to inconsistent contractor compliance and encouraged residents to report issues

- so the City can respond to emerging problems.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED
